comments.text: In Greece, our system is a combination of the private and public sector. We most usually have a general doctor who runs a private office and is paid a rational fee, around 50€ per visit, who prescribes our tests and medicins. The tests are usually made in a private facility, which has an agreement with the state and charges us 10 to 20% of the price. The medicins are purchased at private pharmacies and we pay 25%, except for some drugs that are for chronic conditionw that sometimes have 0% charge. For serious conditions we use the public health care system, meaning hospitals, where we don;t have to pay anything. Most Greeks have an additional private insurance coverage. I for example pay 1,500€ per year and can visit a doctor of the private insurance network for just 10€ and then have my tests done for free. Or go to a private hospital and pay 20% for hospitalization and surgery. But the doctors in the public sector are generally considered better, even if the public infrastacture is not the best or patient friendly. When I had my adrenaline gland removed due to its calcification I chose a public hospital, as the surgeon was considered one of the best in the Balkans, but used my private insurance to give me a financial compasation for the missed workdays. The public sector though does not cover dental expenditure, nor does the private one. Mental health is also a problem in Greece.
